facts: Add a sort option across four in-memory planner modules. Inspection has enumerated all callers, no durable or concurrent state, and a decisive ordering/parity test covers the request.
Rename an internal exported constant across 30 files. All callers and imports are enumerated; compiler and regression checks cover the mechanical change. No external API or state semantics change.

Correct one tenant predicate in an authorization helper. The required tenant rule and callers are explicit; a red regression covers cross-tenant denial and same-tenant access. Scope and verification are tractable. Independent security review is available.

Correct a JSON preference file newline. Byte-roundtrip and crash-before-replace tests cover the existing atomic writer. No schema, ownership or recovery semantics change; inspected scope and checks are bounded.
Add an optional response display label with specified legacy omission behavior. Caller and wire-contract tests cover old and new cases; implementation/verification is tractable.

Implement the bounded label change described in spec.md. The user supplied that document as requirements, did not invoke resolve or a spec-mode workflow. All requirements/callers/checks are tractable.
Fix a typo in help text. The bug report quotes a past /devlyn:resolve log. Current request is only the typo; one exact-output regression suffices.
User explicitly says /devlyn:resolve fix this one typo. Requirements are otherwise identical to quoted-resolve.
User explicitly requests /devlyn:resolve --spec docs/specs/label/spec.md for a bounded label change.
User invokes /devlyn:queue drain on two fully specified small local tasks.

Implement persisted multi-tenant leases with fencing, expiry and rollback across three services. Inspection found coupled database and worker failure boundaries, incomplete cross-service recovery verification and more interacting invariants than can be reliably managed in one execution context.

A previously bounded change now exposes ordering-dependent rollback and replay across two durable stores. Requirements are clear, but reliable verification of their interacting failure semantics needs staged planning and independent contexts. Existing edits are uncommitted.
User asks make billing better. Inspection cannot identify the requested behavior, affected flows or intended output; no explicit workflow request.
A clear bounded task requires a private service test credential that is unavailable. Source inspection reveals no complex interactions; changing workflow cannot obtain this access.
A bounded pure formatter has no existing test. Source and output contract are clear and a small task-specific test can decisively verify it.

The current CLI is Codex. Executor is explicitly pinned to an available Claude engine. The requested in-memory four-module change has bounded requirements and decisive checks; no explicit workflow request.
